docs.title: p2p-lens
docs.text:
Procure-to-pay process intelligence on SAP-style data: process mining, conformance checking, an assumption-driven value model and a citation-grounded Q&A copilot.

Start with the README, then read the architecture and methodology.

All demo numbers come from synthetic data and illustrate the method only.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
synth.generate ──> Dataset (6 tables) ──> eventlog.build_event_log ──> mining.analyze_log
                        │                          │                          │
                        │                          └─> conformance.check_precedence
                        └─> conformance.detect_deviations
                                         │
                                  analysis.analyze  ──>  P2PAnalysis
                                         │
                       findings.build_findings ──> [Finding F01..F11]
                          │            │                 │
                   value.compute_value │          copilot.ask ──> Answer
                          │            │                 (retrieve, LLM?, verify, fallback)
                          └──────> report.* ──> report.md / report.html / charts

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
• One case per purchase order. Simple, explainable, and enough for the deviations modelled. Item-level cases are on the roadmap.
  • Detection from tables, mining from the log. Deviations that need amounts or terms (price mismatch, late payment) use the tables; ordering rules use the event log. Both agree where they overlap (invoice_before_gr equals the goods-receipt-to-invoice precedence violation, asserted in tests).
  • Findings are text built from numbers, not generated. This is what makes grounding checkable.
  • LLM is optional and untrusted. Its output passes a verifier or is discarded.
  • Standard library HTTP. The LLM clients use urllib, so there is no SDK lock-in.
  • Typed and tested. mypy --strict, ruff, and a 90% coverage gate in CI.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Module Responsibility schema.py Table definitions, Dataset, validation, CSV I/O synth.py Seeded generator and GroundTruth eventlog.py Tables to event log; flat CSV loader mining.py Variants, durations, edge waiting times (log only) conformance.py Precedence rules, deviation detectors analysis.py Orchestration, vendors, money figures findings.py Finding model and builders value.py Assumptions, scenarios, ROI copilot.py Retrieval, prompt, grounding check, backends report.py Block model rendered to Markdown or HTML, charts cli.py argparse entry point

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
Six tables, CSV on disk, one row per record. Field names follow SAP where a standard field exists. This is a simplified view, not a full SAP schema.

Table Key fields Notes EKKO (PO header) EBELN, LIFNR, BEDAT, ERNAM, BSART, REL_DATE, ZBD1T, WAERS REL_DATE is the release date; in a real system derive it from release-strategy change documents. ZBD1T is payment-term days. EKPO (PO items) EBELN, EBELP, MATNR, MENGE, NETWR Order value is the sum of NETWR per EBELN. EKBE (PO history) EBELN, BELNR, VGABE, BUDAT, DMBTR VGABE 1 is goods receipt, 2 is invoice receipt. EBAN (requisitions) BANFN, EBELN, BADAT, ERNAM A PO with no EBAN row has no requisition. PO_CHANGES EBELN, UDATE, FNAME, USERNAME In SAP, derive from CDHDR/CDPOS for object class EINKBELEG. PAYMENTS EBELN, AUGDT, DMBTR In SAP, derive from FI clearing (for example BSAK) joined to the PO.

All date columns are timestamps. EBELN is unique in EKKO and every other table must reference it. Dataset.validate() enforces this and the VGABE and ZBD1T constraints.

docs.title: Event log
docs.text:
Activity Source Create Purchase Requisition EBAN.BADAT Create Purchase Order EKKO.BEDAT Release Purchase Order EKKO.REL_DATE Change Purchase Order PO_CHANGES.UDATE Post Goods Receipt EKBE.BUDAT where VGABE = 1 Post Invoice Receipt EKBE.BUDAT where VGABE = 2 Clear Invoice (Payment) PAYMENTS.AUGDT

Columns: case_id, activity, timestamp, resource. Ties on identical timestamps are broken by the canonical activity order.

docs.title: Using real extracts
docs.text: Export the tables to CSV with the column names above and the same file names in lower case (ekko.csv, ekpo.csv, ekbe.csv, eban.csv, po_changes.csv, payments.csv). Dates must parse with pandas.to_datetime. Keep the key columns as text so leading zeros survive.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Synthetic by default. The generator makes the method testable (known ground truth) but cannot show how the tool behaves on real organisational data. Real extracts bring partial deliveries, multi-item receipts, credit memos, cancellations and reversals that are not modelled.
  • One case per purchase order. Item-level and multi-invoice cases are collapsed.
  • Simplified tables. REL_DATE, PO_CHANGES and PAYMENTS are stand-ins for data that, in SAP, must be derived from change documents and FI clearing.
  • Rule-based conformance. Precedence rules and deviation detectors, not alignment against a discovered process model.
  • Strict grounding. The verifier may reject a correct LLM answer that reformats a number.
  • Retrieval is lexical. TF-IDF over a small, fixed set of findings; no embeddings.
  • Value model is assumption-driven. See docs/value-model.md.
  • Tested locally on Python 3.12 with pandas 3.1 and 2.2. CI covers 3.11 to 3.13.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
1. Item-level cases and partial deliveries.
  2. Conformance checking against a discovered model.
  3. Benchmarks on public real-world event logs.
  4. Optional embedding retrieval behind the same grounding check.

docs.title: Deviation definitions
docs.text: Deviation Definition no_pr The purchase order has no requisition row. rework At least one change event after creation. invoice_before_gr First invoice receipt is earlier than first goods receipt. price_mismatch The first invoice differs from the order value by more than 5% (configurable). duplicate_invoice Two or more invoice documents for the order with the same amount (rounded to cents). late_payment Payment clearing is later than first invoice date plus ZBD1T days.

docs.title: Process-mining measures
docs.text:
• Variant: the ordered activity sequence of a case. Share and cumulative share are reported.
  • Case duration: last event minus first event, in days.
  • Waiting time: for each pair of consecutive events in a case, the elapsed days; summarised per directly-follows pair (count, mean, median, p90, total case-days).
  • Bottleneck ranking: by total case-days, excluding the invoice-to-payment wait, which is determined by contractual payment terms rather than by process friction.

docs.title: Conformance
docs.text: Five precedence rules (requisition before order, order before release, release before goods receipt, goods receipt before invoice, invoice before payment) are checked on the first occurrence of each activity. A case conforms when it breaks no rule and contains all mandatory activities (order, release, goods receipt, invoice, payment). A missing requisition is reported separately as no_pr and does not break conformance.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The generator injects each deviation from an explicit per-case flag and records the exact count. The analysis never sees the flags. Tests assert the counts match exactly for four seeds.

docs.title: Grounding check
docs.text: Given an answer and the retrieved findings: (1) it must contain at least one [Fnn] citation, (2) every cited id must be one of the retrieved findings, (3) every number in the answer (after removing citations and list markers) must appear in a cited finding or in the question. Numbers are compared as floats after removing thousands separators. The check is intentionally strict: a correct answer that rounds a number differently falls back to the extractive answer rather than risk an unsupported figure.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Measured with python benchmarks/benchmark.py 10000 50000 100000 on a single run in a Linux sandbox (Python 3.12, pandas 3.1). Your numbers will differ; the shape (linear scaling) is the point.

Cases Events Generate Analyze Findings Detection equals ground truth Peak memory 10,000 61,378 1.5 s 0.4 s 0.002 s yes 123 MB 50,000 307,294 9.9 s 1.9 s 0.002 s yes 308 MB 100,000 614,690 19.7 s 4.3 s 0.002 s yes 580 MB

Peak memory includes the generator and all tables held in memory. Analysis is vectorised pandas (group-bys and shifts), so it scales roughly linearly with the number of events.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Everything is in memory. Logs of tens of millions of events need chunking or a database, which is out of scope.
  • The generator is a Python loop and is meant for tests and demos, not for load testing.

docs.title: Concept map: p2p-lens and commercial process-mining platforms
docs.text:
Commercial platforms and this project share the same ideas. This table is a conceptual map written from public documentation of common process-mining terms, not a statement about any vendor's exact feature set or syntax.

Concept In p2p-lens Event log (case, activity, timestamp) eventlog.build_event_log Variant explorer mining.variant_table Throughput time mining.case_durations, finding F01 Bottleneck between steps mining.edge_table, finding F09 Conformance checking conformance.check_precedence, detect_deviations Automation or touchless rate Share of cases on the reference path, finding F02 Value realisation value.compute_value with explicit assumptions Data model from source tables schema.Dataset and docs/data-model.md Data ingestion (activity table + case table) export.export_tables (p2p-lens export) Mapping a source system's activities to a reference process conformance.load_activity_map (--p2p-map) Business case / opportunity sizing Executive summary in the report, value.compute_value

docs.title: Running on a real public event log
docs.text: analyze-log reads IEEE XES (.xes, .xes.gz) and flat CSV files. XES parsing uses defusedxml, so a hostile file cannot trigger entity-expansion attacks (covered by a test).

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
The pm4py project ships a real-world log in its test data (activity names match the receipt-phase log of an environmental-permit process from the CoSeLoG project, as distributed on 4TU.ResearchData). It is not bundled here because redistribution terms should be checked at the source.

curl -L -o receipt.xes \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pm4py/pm4py-core/release/tests/input_data/receipt.xes
p2p-lens analyze-log --log receipt.xes --out receipt-report

Result when run on 2026-11-22: 1,434 cases and 8,577 events. Median case duration is under one hour, p90 is 14.1 days, the longest case is 275.8 days, and the reference sequence covers 49.7% of cases. The largest waiting-time contributor is the step from "T05 Print and send confirmation of receipt" to "T06 Determine necessity of stop advice" (mean 3.1 days, p90 8.0 days).

This is a general process-mining run. The SAP-specific deviation detectors and value model need the purchasing tables (see data-model.md), so they are not part of analyze-log.

docs.title: Running the P2P checks on a real log
docs.text:
Real logs name their activities differently. Copy examples/p2p-map.example.yaml, list your log's activity names under each role, and run:

p2p-lens analyze-log --log yourlog.xes --p2p-map map.yaml --out out

The report gains a section with precedence violations (for example invoice before goods receipt) and a conformance rate over the mapped events. The mechanism is tested by renaming the activities of a synthetic log and recovering the injected invoice-before-goods-receipt count exactly. Item-level logs treat each item as a case, so read the rates accordingly.

docs.title: BPI Challenge logs
docs.text: BPI Challenge event logs (for example the 2019 purchase-order log) are distributed as XES on 4TU.ResearchData. Download one there, accept its licence, and pass the file to analyze-log. That specific log has not been run through this tool yet.

docs.title: CSV logs
docs.text: p2p-lens analyze-log --log my.csv --case-col case --activity-col act --timestamp-col ts --out out

docs.title: Value model
docs.text: The value model multiplies observed rates by assumptions you control. It is a way to make a business case explicit and challengeable, not a forecast.

docs.title: Levers
docs.text:
Lever Problem size (before any program) Rework handling reworked cases x changes per case x cost per change Late-payment fees value of late invoices x late-fee rate Duplicate-invoice leakage value of duplicate invoices x interception rate Overbilling recovery positive price differences on mismatched invoices x recovery rate

Each problem size is scaled from the observed volume to --annual-cases (default: observed volume annualised from the data span), then multiplied by each scenario's share (conservative, base, optimistic) to give an annual benefit.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: annual_benefit_eur, roi_year1_pct = (benefit - program cost) / program cost and payback_months = 12 x program cost / benefit per scenario.

docs.title: Read this before quoting a number
docs.text:
• Every assumption in default_assumptions.yaml is a placeholder. Replace them with figures from the organisation concerned.
  • On synthetic data the result only demonstrates the mechanics. For example, scaling the demo run to 150,000 orders a year produces very large ratios because the placeholder program cost is small relative to the scaled spend. That says something about the placeholders, not about any company.
  • Benefits are not additive proof: levers can overlap, and none accounts for implementation risk.
